chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala'a ibn Razin, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The virgins who have a father cannot be married off except by the permission of their fathers.

key_terms.الْأَبْكَارِ: virgins (females who have not been married)
key_terms.تَزَوَّجُ: she is married / they are married off

ai.seo_question: What is the requirement for marrying a virgin daughter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the father's permission (idhn) as a mandatory condition (shart) for the validity of a virgin daughter's marriage, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the father holds the right of guardianship (wilayah) over his unmarried daughter. While some schools consider it a prerequisite for validity, others view it as a right of the father that can be waived, highlighting the nuanced scholarly debate on paternal authority in marital contracts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ala’a Bin Razeyn, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The virgins who are with a father cannot get married except by the permission of their fathers’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from ibn abu ibn abu Ya’fur who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A virgin woman who has her father must not marry without his permission.’”
